title: KV lifespan economics and batching synthesis: policy recommendations and safe rollout
creator: Alex Kim
description: Goal: produce a reproducible set of KV/prefix caching recommendations that jointly optimize cost and latency by combining hit-rate economics, lifespan (expiry) tuning, and batch-sensitivity-aware cache key design. Deliverables: 1) runtime-safe recommendation engine and config templates for per-prefix lifespan and batching parameters; 2) an offline simulator and a shadowing harness to validate; 3) an automated staged apply + rollback orchestration with explicit safety gates and dashboards. Background: our current autotuners use per-prefix heuristics that treat expiry (TTL) and batch sizes independently, which leads to suboptimal decisions for workloads with variable prefix locality and request size distributions. This work ties together a small, explainable econometric model with practical rollout controls.
problem_statement: We need to reduce per-token serving cost without regressions in observed latency percentiles or correctness. Existing heuristics either over-retain keys (wasting memory and incorrect cache pressure) or aggressively expire keys (losing hit-rate and increasing token generation). There is no unified signal that quantifies monetary trade-offs when changing lifespan or cache key granularity. Additionally, batch-size sensitivity changes effective hit-rate and must be accounted for in recommendations.
approach_summary: 1) Build hit-rate econometric model that estimates marginal token savings from raising per-prefix lifespan; 2) Use workload-aware batching model to compute effective hit probability when batched; 3) Produce per-prefix configs (lifespan, key-morphing rules, batching hints) with expected cost delta and confidence intervals; 4) Validate with offline replay + shadow canary; 5) Stage apply with progressive ramp and automatic rollback based on SLO/cost thresholds.
cost_model: We define expected_net_savings(prefix) = (delta_hit_rate * avg_saved_tokens_per_hit * token_cost) - additional_memory_cost(prefix) - batching_overhead_cost. Where delta_hit_rate is modeled from historical prefix inter-arrival distribution using a survival model. avg_saved_tokens_per_hit is estimated from past request length percentiles. token_cost is derived from runtime unit economics. Additional_memory_cost(prefix) = memory_bytes * memory_cost_per_byte_per_hour * expected_retention_hours. We will surface per-prefix ROI and a recommended min-confidence threshold (default 95%) before applying a change.
recommendations_summary:
- Lifespan (expiry) should be expressed as an economic policy per prefix bucket (e.g., short/medium/long) rather than a single TTL for all keys.
- Key design: prefer 'affix-collapsed' keys for high-cardinality prefixes that show low reuse; use stricter canonicalization for stable prefixes where affinity benefits batching and cache reuse.
- Batching: annotate routes with 'batch-sensitivity' score; avoid increasing lifespan for prefixes where batching reduces effective hit-rate (e.g., requests with highly diverse prefixes in one batch).
- Safety: require ROI>0.5x payback in 24h at 95% CI before applying to hosted tier; lower bar for internal sandbox traffic.
safe_apply_and_rollback: Staged apply plan: 1) dry-run in simulation (no config change) and generate expected metrics; 2) shadow canary (apply to 0% traffic but collect cache metrics); 3) progressive rollout: 0.5% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with 30-minute observation windows and health checks. Automatic rollback triggers: A) >=5% relative regression in p99 latency for any region versus baseline; B) >=10% drop in end-to-end success rate for affected routes; C) observed actual cost savings deviates from predicted by more than 50% negative. Rollback mechanism: orchestration will revert configs and schedule a postmortem job; changes are idempotent and support fast reapply if subsequent fixes are made.
telemetry_and_alerting: Essential signals: per-prefix hit-rate (1m and 5m), prefix cardinality, avg tokens saved per hit, memory consumption per node, p50/p95/p99 latency, downstream error rate, token spend per route. Dashboards: economic dashboard (predicted vs actual savings), safety dashboard (latency/error windows), rollout timeline. Alerts: numeric thresholds mapped to rollback triggers plus a human-notify slack channel #kv-rollouts.
offline_validation: Notebook: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-lifespan-sim (notebook + synthetic replay). Steps: 1) replay 30d sampled traffic with candidate lifespan changes; 2) compute delta_hit_rate, delta_memory, delta_tokens; 3) run bootstrapped confidence intervals. Acceptance for shadow: model-predicted savings within 20% of replay-estimated savings.
shadow_and_canary: Harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-shadow (service to replicate requests and maintain separate cache instance). Canary schedule and metrics collection are implemented as part of runtime orchestration. Shadow must run for a minimum of 48h with representative traffic before any public rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Automated simulator reproduces historical hit-rate within 10% MAE for top-500 prefixes by traffic.
Shadow run for 48h with no safety triggers fired for growth scenarios and synthetic bursts.
Runbook and rollback automation implemented and tested in staging with end-to-end recovery verified.
Per-prefix recommendations annotated with expected ROI and 95% CI in the console UI.
Cost dashboard shows a clear mapping of applied policy to realized token savings within 30% of prediction over first 7 days.
Docs and runbook available for SRE and customer support teams.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Simulation and config generator (owner: ENG)
Phase 1: Shadow canary on internal traffic for 48h (owner: ENG)
Phase 2: Staged public canary: 0.5% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% (owner: ENG + SRE)
Phase 3: Monitor 7-day drift and optionally expand policy scope (owner: PM + ENG)
Phase 4: Postmortem and lessons learned (owner: ENG)
Rollback: automatic triggers + manual rollback runbook in Console (SRE on-call)
testing_plan: Unit tests for econometric model and CI for confidence intervals
Integration tests: simulator vs production replay dataset (sanitized)
Chaos test: simulate sudden prefix cardinality explosion and verify safe-apply halts
End-to-end: apply change to staging runtime and validate automated rollback on safety triggers
metrics_and_targets: Primary: net token spend reduction >= 6% for targeted workload slice within 7 days
Safety: no more than 2% relative increase in p95 latency for any route
Reliability: end-to-end success rate change <= 0.5% absolute
Model accuracy: predicted savings vs replayed savings MAE <= 30% on first 7-day window
notes: Trade-offs considered: conservative lifespan increases reduce immediate ROI but limit long-tail regressions; aggressive key coalescing increases cache pressure for certain multi-tenant workloads.
We chose to expose economic thresholds rather than raw TTL values in the first iteration to keep operator intent explicit.
Potential future work: integrate model with Optimize to suggest quantization profiles together with caching for combined cost wins.
